title: Heat Pump Water Heater Rebates in Kelowna 2026: Up to $1,000
desc: Kelowna's electricity comes from FortisBC, so FortisBC pays up to $1,000 for a heat pump water heater replacing a standard electric tank. 65% of households own. Rules and installers.
h1: Heat Pump Water Heater Rebates in Kelowna
lead: Kelowna's electricity comes from FortisBC, so FortisBC pays the heat pump water heater rebate. It is $1,000 for replacing a standard electric storage tank.
cards_heading: What heat pump water heater rebates pay in Kelowna
cards_intro: We read FortisBC's heat pump water heater listing on October 2, 2026. It pays $1,000 when you replace a standard electric storage tank. If you are switching from another fuel, FortisBC points to CleanBC instead.

cards.title: FortisBC
cards.note: For replacing a standard electric storage tank with a high-efficiency heat pump water heater.

cards.title: Second-upgrade bonus
cards.note: FortisBC adds $300 for a second upgrade, or an EnerGuide improvement bonus of $750 to $2,000.

cards.title: Income-qualified (CleanBC)
cards.note: Level 1 households replacing a fossil-fuel or electric water heater. Level 2 gets up to $2,800 from electric. Primary water heater only.

cards.title: Lower incomes (FortisBC)
cards.note: Income-qualified customers can get free evaluations and upgrades.

after_cards:
A Kelowna house

Replacing a standard electric tank earns $1,000 from FortisBC. Adding 12 windows and a door earns 13 x $100 = $1,300. Together $2,300 before any bonus.
sections: Who in Kelowna can use this

The 2021 Census counted 62,210 households in Kelowna. About 65% own, 43% live in detached houses and 33% in apartments. Of the households, 8,205 own a detached house built before 1981. Kelowna's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was -3.2°C.

This is the rule that surprises people. Heat pump water heater rebates from BC Hydro and FortisBC start with an electric tank. A gas tank swap is a different case, and households above the income limits have no rebate for it. Income-qualified households can apply to CleanBC, which pays up to $3,500 at Level 1. Only one primary water heating rebate is allowed per home, so you cannot collect from two programs for the same tank.

BC Hydro pays only for models that sit in Tier 2 or higher on NEEA's Advanced Water Heater Specification list for heat pump water heaters. Ask the installer for the exact model number and check it against the list before you sign. Put the model on the invoice. A tank that is not on the list will not be paid, no matter how efficient it looks.

You have six months from the invoice date to apply. The only supporting document is the invoice, and BC Hydro publishes a sample showing what it must list. The installer must be a licensed contractor with a GST number and a valid BC business licence for the trade. Self-installation is not eligible, and the new tank must not have been used in another home.

BC Hydro's rebate needs a BC Hydro account, and Kelowna households buy power from FortisBC. FortisBC lists the heat pump water heater rebate for customers who replace a standard electric storage tank. If you are switching from another energy source, FortisBC points you to its partners at CleanBC.
installers_intro: These are the top-rated heat pump and HVAC companies near Kelowna by Google reviews, weighted by number of reviews. Ask whether each one installs heat pump water heaters before you book. Nobody pays to be listed.
claim_steps: Check that the tank you are replacing is electric and is your primary water heater.
Pick a model from NEEA's Tier 2 or higher list and get it on the quote.
Have a licensed contractor install it and keep the invoice.
Apply online within six months of the invoice date.
If your income is lower, ask about the CleanBC program before paying.
faq: Do I apply to BC Hydro in Kelowna?
No. FortisBC supplies Kelowna's electricity, so apply to FortisBC.
What does my existing tank need to be?
A standard electric storage tank model.
What if my tank is gas?
FortisBC points you to CleanBC, which pays up to $3,500 for income-qualified households.
FortisBC lists $300 for a second upgrade, or an EnerGuide improvement bonus of $750 to $2,000.
